eve_support: Customer reports repeated JSON parse failures when using JSON/structured mode with streaming enabled. They say some responses contain raw tab characters (0x09) that arrive unescaped and crash their parser. Pasted redacted request + error from customer below.

eve_support: ---- customer payload (redacted) ----
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b", "structured": {"mode":"json"}, "stream": true, "prompt": "line1\\tline2"}'

customer error (their parser):
JSONDecodeError: Invalid control character at: line 1 column 73 (char 72)
---- end pasted ----

sam_support: Can you get the customer's request-id and the exact response bytes (hex or raw capture)? Also which SDK/version or curl? If streaming true, client-side chunk reassembly could be dropping a backslash.

eve_support: request-id: req_01H2X9QY (customer-provided). They used curl in a containerized environment and said the failing parse happens intermittently. Attached a tiny log they sent: 

--- log snippet ---
received chunk: "...\\\"prompt\\\": \"hello\\two...\"
received chunk: "...\"prompt\": \"hello\two...\"
--- end ---

They suspect a proxy or sidecar rewriting escape sequences.

charlie_engineer: This looks like streaming chunk boundary issues where the backslash escape (\\t) gets split across TCP chunks and the client reassembly step (or a proxy) is un-escaping prematurely so the parser sees an actual tab byte. Two quick asks:
1) customer raw response capture (pcap or curl --raw output / hexdump)
2) confirm whether they have any reverse proxies doing content-modifying transforms (nginx lua, envoy filters, etc).

charlie_engineer: Workarounds we can ask customer to try immediately:
- disable streaming (stream=false) to confirm this is streaming-related
- if they must stream, post-process the stream to escape control chars (replace 0x09 with \t) before handing to strict JSON parser

sam_support: Also check if their container runtime or logging agent is "pretty printing" strings. I've seen sidecars that unescape sequences when forwarding logs.

maria_sre: From infra side: please capture raw bytes and include Content-Encoding and any gateway/transcoding hops. If this is a proxy rewrite, we can correlate with edge logs (edge-request-id: req_01H2X9QY) and see if a chunk was modified midflight.

eve_support: Customer sent a small repro that toggles stream on/off. Repro steps (from customer):
1) run the curl above with stream=true in their k8s cluster
2) collect stdout and hexdump: `curl ... | xxd`
They attached `xxd` output showing 0x09 bytes inside the JSON string occasionally.

charlie_engineer: I pushed a local reproducer that simulates chunk-splitting escape sequences. Node example to reproduce (small chunks):
```js
// simulate server sending split chunks that break escape sequences
const http = require('http');
http.createServer((req, res) => {
  res.write('{"choices":[{"text":"line1\\\\');
  setTimeout(() => { res.write('tline2"}]}'); res.end(); }, 20);
}).listen(3000);
// client that streams and attempts JSON.parse on incremental buffer will fail if it sees raw 0x09
```

charlie_engineer: Short-term fix: ensure our streaming layer always emits escapes as `\\t` or uses `\\u0009` for control characters. I'll open an internal ticket to harden the streaming encoder.

maria_sre: If we're going to patch encoder we need an ops plan: can we make it a safe opt-in first? Example rollout: canary -> 24h -> full. Also need to check compatibility with existing clients.

charlie_engineer: Opening internal issue ENG-JSON-6821, P1 for customer impact. I'll include reproducer and a proposed encoder change to always escape tabs and newlines as `\\t` / `\\n` in streamed chunks.

eve_support: Sent customer a short repro checklist and asked for raw capture + confirmation they can try stream=false. Waiting on customer.

deploy-bot: Canary job scheduled for branch `json-escape-fix` (job id canary-772).

sam_support: Thanks — keep me posted. If customer confirms they can reproduce with stream=false = no failure, that strongly points at streaming chunk boundary.

eve_support: Will update when customer responds. :thumbsup:
